subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: Should Telegram automatically reset or partition polling offsets when `channels.telegram.apiRoot` changes, and should polling startup tolerate `400: Logged out` only during configured local Bot API migration?
rationale: The remaining fix changes persisted polling-state semantics and startup failure handling, and an overly broad `400` tolerance could hide real auth/config errors.

options.title: Endpoint-aware migration
options.body: Store or derive endpoint identity for update offsets, clear incompatible offsets through runtime or doctor-owned migration, and add a narrowly matched `Logged out` cleanup tolerance with live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Documented manual reset
options.body: Leave runtime behavior strict and document an explicit operator reset sequence for switching Bot API roots, accepting a more technical recovery path.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed behavior
options.body: Treat local Bot API migration as advanced unsupported edge behavior beyond the current `apiRoot` passthrough and keep startup/error semantics unchanged.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware migration
recommendation.body: Store or derive endpoint identity for update offsets, clear incompatible offsets through runtime or doctor-owned migration, and add a narrowly matched `Logged out` cleanup tolerance with live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and prior Telegram offset work make this the best available routing candidate for the persisted polling-state decision.
